Leonardo de Pisa, llamado Fibonacci, pla: Leonardo of Pisa, called Fibonacci, set out in 1202, in his Liber abaci, a problem about rabbits breeding each month, and the sequence came out of it. The book served above all to introduce Hindu-Arabic numerals into Europe. Generating functions were invented by Abraham de Moivre around 1730, precisely to solve recurrences, and Binet's formula, which bears Jacques Binet's name because of an 1843 paper, was already known to de Moivre and Euler a century earlier.

Muchas sucesiones no se definen con una: Many sequences are not defined with a formula for term $n$, but by saying how each term is computed from the previous ones. It is what in [[fn-sucesiones]] was called a definition by recurrence. The most famous is Fibonacci's: each term is the sum of the two before it. But they turn up everywhere: in growing populations, in loans being paid off and, above all, in counting how long an algorithm that calls itself takes. To solve them a quadratic equation and a system of two equations are enough.
